claim.why_it_matters: The flowchart's connectors are lost: the markdown lists box labels and a two-cell table, so it no longer states that every 'yes' branch leads to 'Truth value is false' and only the final 'no' leads to 'true' (the AND short-circuit the figure illustrates). Informative annex.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered printed page 796 (PDF p818) at 300 dpi. The figure shows Evaluate condition-1 -> rounded decision 'Condition-1 false'; its 'yes' exit goes right to a vertical line on the right; 'no' continues down to Evaluate condition-2 -> 'Condition-2 false' (yes joins the same right line, no continues) -> Evaluate condition-n -> 'Condition-n false' (yes joins the right line, which ends in an arrow to 'Truth value is false'; no arrows down to 'Truth value is true'). The markdown (page-818.md) keeps only the box and branch labels as loose paragraphs ('Condition-1 yes\ false', 'no', ...) and a two-column table 'Truth value | Truth value / is true | is false'. No connector or routing is stated, so the transcription does not say where any yes/no branch goes: the figure's whole content (any false condition makes the AND false; only all-true reaches true) is lost. The claim quotes both sources accurately. Labels are present, so nothing textual is missing; the loss is the diagram's structure. Informative annex E, so no normative impact, but a genuine content loss of the figure.
